name: Sema - Read, Write, and Thrive with Dyslexia
description: Dyslexia-friendly reading, writing and screen help

paragraphs: Sema helps people who find reading hard. It was built for my brother, who has dyslexia, and for anyone who struggles with everyday text — a letter, a bill, a form, a screen. Most AI today lives in giant data centres. Sema is the opposite: it runs entirely on small, open models (all well under 32B parameters), the kind you could run on hardware you own. Small models, real help.
Every model Sema uses is open and under the 32B cap:

SnapGuide is built around MiniCPM-V from OpenBMB — the recommended small vision model for image, OCR and document understanding — which is exactly what helping someone read a screen or form requires. A Qwen3-VL vision model is wired in as an automatic fallback so the app keeps working even if the MiniCPM endpoint is busy. The whole app is accessibility-first: dyslexia-friendly font and spacing, audio for everything, voice input, plain-language output, and Kiswahili support so it reaches people that English-only tools leave out.
